parts.note: read plainly, any showy or over-elaborate manner
the setter means the ornate eighteenth-century decorative fashion full of scrolls and shells

explanation.definitionFit: The name of the ornate eighteenth-century European art movement is now used for anything fussily over-decorated.

parts.note: read plainly, a verb for going down or refusing
the setter means a verb for withdrawing or diminishing, as floodwaters or hairlines do

explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: floodwaters, hairlines and fears all diminish and draw back gradually over time.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turns from liquid into a semi-solid mass
second meaning: becomes denser, as sour milk does

explanation.definitionFit: Milk going sour separates into lumpy solids, a process described by both verbs in the clue.

definitions.note: the question mark flags the clue as an example of the nationality, not a full definition

parts.note: read plainly, a phrase describing where someone or something originates
the setter means the adjective for the country whose capital that city is

explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic, so anything originating there carries this national adjective.

parts.note: read plainly, a general-knowledge question about a famous American
the setter wants the given name of the general who became the thirty-fourth US president

explanation.definitionFit: The Allied supreme commander and later US president was christened with this given name, nicknamed Ike.

parts.note: read plainly, an adjective or a noun for a warning
the setter means the adjective for not sleeping and watchful

explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone who stays awake and vigilant through the night is watchful and attentive.

parts.note: read plainly, any nation on that side of the continent
the setter means the equatorial nation whose capital is Libreville

explanation.definitionFit: This equatorial republic on the Atlantic coast, capital Libreville, lies in the western part of the continent.

parts.note: read plainly, these letters suggest a disc jockey playing records
the setter means the British abbreviation for dinner jacket

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain DJ is short for dinner jacket as well as disc jockey; it is the formal jacket that is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner jacket is the formal black evening suit jacket, called by the American name in the answer.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a malevolent magical invocation
second meaning: a swear word or profanity

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a witch's malevolent hex and a profane exclamation uttered in anger.

parts.note: read plainly, any music machine you pay to use
the setter means the familiar café and bar machine that plays a chosen single

explanation.definitionFit: Cafés and bars once housed these machines, which played a selected single after customers inserted money.

parts.words: Swing out of control (as trailer of lorry)
parts.note: the setter means a verb named after a folding pocket blade, for an articulated vehicle folding sharply

explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulated truck whose trailer skids round to form a sharp angle with the cab resembles a folding pocket blade.

parts.note: read plainly, a description of unclear prophecy
the setter means the adjective from the Greek shrine of Apollo, famed for riddling prophecies

explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek shrine of Apollo gave notoriously riddling prophecies, so its adjective now means obscure.

parts.note: read plainly, a description of a court ruling
the setter means a single past participle for being punished with a monetary charge

explanation.definitionFit: Someone whom a court or authority punishes with a monetary charge has received this sanction.

parts.note: read plainly, anything that sets something burning
the setter means the engine component that fires the fuel mixture in each cylinder

explanation.definitionFit: In a petrol engine this component produces an electric flash that fires the fuel mixture in each cylinder.

parts.note: read plainly, a verb form for consuming food
the setter means a phrase for being seated for a meal

explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting down for a meal with family or guests is described by this phrase.

parts.note: read plainly, any chick or fledgling
the setter means the offspring of a goose

explanation.definitionFit: This word names a baby goose, a fluffy waterfowl chick, so it is one specific juvenile bird.

parts.note: read plainly, any old-fashioned string for a fiddle
the setter means the cord made from dried sheep intestine

explanation.definitionFit: Before steel and nylon, instrument strings were made from twisted dried sheep intestine, known by this name.

parts.note: read plainly, could suggest part of a photograph or a drink
the setter means one small lead ball from a shotgun cartridge

explanation.definitionFit: Shotgun cartridges contain many small lead balls, each one called by this name.

parts.note: read plainly, a phrase about expecting something
the setter means a single verb for waiting for something to come

explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate or expect an event, staying ready until it arrives, is expressed by this verb.

parts.note: read plainly, a request for a translation
the setter means the French word for love, used in English for a sweetheart or affair

explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, this word means a love affair or a sweetheart, especially a secret one.

parts.note: read plainly, an adverb for speed
the setter means a two-word phrase for doing something hurriedly

explanation.definitionFit: A prepositional phrase meaning hurriedly, often with the sense of too fast to be careful.

parts.note: read plainly, any pedestrian
the setter means a person on a long country trek carrying gear

explanation.definitionFit: A person trekking long distances through the countryside on foot, usually carrying supplies, is called this.

parts.note: read plainly, a parting word or occasion
the setter means the everyday expression said when leaving

explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the usual expression people say when parting from each other or leaving a place.

parts.note: read plainly, any shellfish eaten by marine mammals
the setter means the tiny shrimp-like plankton that baleen whales filter from seawater

explanation.definitionFit: These tiny shrimp-like plankton swarm in polar seas and are filtered in vast quantities by baleen whales.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the large fowl eaten at Christmas and Thanksgiving
second meaning: the nation straddling Europe and Asia with Ankara as capital
third meaning: slang for a theatrical or commercial failure

explanation.definitionFit: One word names a festive fowl, the nation centred on Anatolia, and slang for a disastrous show or film.

parts.note: read plainly, could suggest a bell or siren going off
the setter means an abrupt feeling of fear

explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an abrupt shock of fear, such as being startled by an unexpected noise.
